RT by @solana_devs: Solana explorers tell you what a transaction did. Test frameworks show how a program behaves in isolation.

But what if you could take a real mainnet transaction and ask: what if it had gone differently?

That's svmscope.

Paste any signature and it reconstructs the accounts the transaction touched and the program binaries it invoked, then re-executes it in LiteSVM — an in-process SVM running the real program code, no mocks.

From there, rewrite the world it ran in. Edit an account field, change a balance, or move the clock forward — then replay and watch how the programs respond. Break an oracle assumption. Zero out a vault. Jump a vesting cliff and watch a claim that reverts today succeed 90 days later.

No validator. No full-network fork. About a second per run.

Find a case worth keeping? Export the whole state as a hermetic fixture — a deterministic regression test you can run offline or in CI.

Decode → replay → mutate → assert.

Free, open source, and still in beta. Paste your gnarliest transaction and see what you can break — safely, in an isolated sandbox.

https://svmscope.vercel.app/
